findings.claim: Basis: a scratch copy of the frozen loop-4 export (HEAD 3c6a03a2; lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 9278b451); within the lab directory only tests/lab.mjs differs from the loop-3 export. npm ci in tests, Node v24.2.0. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic's own solution (built by the critic's loop-3 builder script: the starter with the critic's compose, Dockerfile, handler and workflow edits, and the worksheet filled from the public rule file) passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT, and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. Variants are one-change edits of that solution: the loop-3 critic suite (110 variants) plus 38 new loop-4 variants and controls, each run under node --test with LAB_PROJECT and by calling every exported rule in tests/lab.mjs, with identical pass counts; the loop-2 suite (117 folders) was rerun through the exported rules. All of these were also graded by the loop-3 grader: across the loop-3 and loop-2 suites exactly six variants differ (three guard-message changes, the cat heredoc piped into docker login, and the annotated and chained clients), each in the direction the loop-3 reconciliation asks for. Python variants (all but a no-httpx control, whose other library is not installed) ran under FastAPI TestClient with httpx 0.28.1 against a local stub api; run blocks ran under bash 3.2.57 with -e and with -eo pipefail, a stub docker and a dummy value. New false failure introduced by the loop-4 binding pattern. Line 300 now allows a colon and annotation text between the bound name and the equals sign, and the match starts at the leftmost name on the line. On a one-line compound statement the colon of the statement header is read as an annotation, so the client is recorded under the word before that colon. Reproduced as a one-change variant of the critic's solution: a module-level client built with base_url set to API_BASE_URL and the Timeout, bound by a plain assignment written as the body of a one-line if statement (the condition, a colon and the assignment on one line), whose get takes the relative path and a dict-literal header. The loop-3 grader passes it 26/26; the loop-4 grader fails tests 24 and 25 with "make the call to the shop api with httpx, as the starter does" (line 343) and "no httpx request to the shop api was found" (line 399). Runtime (FastAPI TestClient, httpx 0.28.1, stub api): it forwards the caller's token and answers 401 without one, so both messages are false. Applied to the text alone, the pattern likewise returns the header word for else, try and with headers followed by an assignment on the same line, where the loop-3 pattern returned the assigned name. Severity low: PEP 8 discourages compound statements, and no page, starter or README form uses one; the annotated, plain, with-as and walrus bindings all pass.
findings.recommendation: Anchor the binding pattern at the start of the logical statement: an optional compound-statement header ending in a colon, then the name, then an optional annotation that contains no colon, then a single equals sign. Or take the bound name as the last identifier before the annotation colon that directly precedes the equals sign.

New false passes introduced by the loop-4 heredoc join. The joined opening command (line 642) is cut only at ;, && and || (line 638), and the exemption (line 666) checks only that the last pipe stage is docker login --password-stdin. Reproduced as one-change variants of the critic's solution, each 26/26 on the loop-4 grader and failing only test 7 on the loop-3 grader: (1) the login step's run with cat opening an unquoted heredoc of the variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD, sent to the background with a single &, then on the same line the README echo-into-login pipeline; (2) the README form followed by cat opening the same heredoc with its standard output redirected to stderr and piped into docker login --password-stdin. Under bash 3.2.57 with -e and with -eo pipefail, a stub docker and a dummy value, both write the value to the log, and in (2) docker receives empty input. Both are h1 under the loop-3 reconciliation's reading, so ops-sme-r2-03, ops-sme-r1-07 and ops-sme-r3-02 are held open on them, and ops-sme-003 on its universal must-fail sentence. The non-heredoc analogs (an echo of the variable sent to the background before the README pipeline, and an echo redirected to stderr and piped into docker login) pass on both graders, because commands() (line 578) also omits & and the pipeline exemption (lines 653-660) also ignores redirects; those predate loop 4 and are not counted here. A cat tee to stderr inside the heredoc pipeline is still flagged by the pipeline check (line 658). Severity low: neither shape is taught, both need a deliberate & or redirect, and the README form passes.
findings.recommendation: In heredocs(), also cut the joined command at a single & that is a list operator (not part of &&, >&, &> or |&); and before skipping a cat-opened body as fed to docker login, require that the cat stage has no standard-output redirect (>, >>, 1>, >&2, &>). The same two guards could be applied to commands() and the pipeline exemption.
